testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When you start the vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Decrease.
Rise slowly.
Stay the same.
Jump quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slowly.
questions.explanation: After you start your vehicle, watch the temperature gauge. The coolant temperature should gradually increase to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Not use the brakes.
Put the vehicle in reverse.
Turn the steering wheel hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not use the brakes. Instead, take your foot off the gas and push in the clutch. This will slow your vehicle and help it regain grip on the road.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Count on traffic control signals.
Never try to drive faster than a train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never try to drive faster than a train.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a railroad crossing. You may not hear a train coming, and signals may not warn you in time. Never try to outrun a train at a railroad crossing.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, your brakes may fade. What happens when brakes fade?

options.text: They become quieter.
They work less well.
They work better than usual.
They work differently in front and back.

questions.correctAnswerText: They work less well.
questions.explanation: Using your brakes too much on a steep downhill can make them overheat and work less well. To avoid brake problems on a steep hill, use engine braking instead.

questions.question: When other drivers cannot see your vehicle well, such as at dawn or dusk, you can help by:

options.text: Keeping your lights off.
Turning your lights on.
Driving on the shoulder.
Waving your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your lights on.
questions.explanation: When it is hard to see, turn on your headlights to low beam. If you cannot see others, they probably cannot see you either.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful, since you cannot control what is far ahead.
Good practice to spot hazards early.
Not allowed.
Only needed if you are carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Good practice to spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards early and react safely.

questions.question: A vehicle's center of gravity height:

options.text: Does not affect how the vehicle handles.
Affects how safely you can handle the vehicle.
Should not matter when loading cargo.
Only matters if your route has many hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Affects how safely you can handle the vehicle.
questions.explanation: The center of gravity height is very important to safe handling. Keep cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: To park as safely as possible, you should park so you can:

options.text: Back out to leave.
Pull forward to leave.
Park on the roadside instead of a lot.
Back into your space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward to leave.
questions.explanation: Backing is risky, so avoid it when you can. Park so you can drive forward when leaving.

questions.question: When you start the engine during the pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Listen for strange sounds.
Rev the engine.
Turn up the radio.
Turn on the heater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for strange sounds.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, listen carefully for any unusual noises.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Should not be used.
Protect the driver from cargo moving forward.
Help protect the driver's head when entering the truck cab.
Provide extra storage space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo moving forward.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before starting a trip
While driving
After a trip
Mirrors do not need to be adjusted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting a trip
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: If something is unsafe during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Continue with the trip and make an appointment with a mechanic after the trip is completed.
Let a more experienced driver use the truck.
Get the issue fixed immediately.
Not use the items found to be unsafe, but may continue driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get the issue fixed immediately.
questions.explanation: You must get the unsafe part fixed right away. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if brakes become too hot?

options.text: They will become too smooth.
They will harden.
They may stop working.
The air compressor will kick in to cool the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: They may stop working.
questions.explanation: If brakes overheat from too much use, they may stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: How can you tell if a vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: A sticker on the control panel.
A yellow lamp on the instrument panel.
The letters "ABS" on the brake pedal.
A metal plate on the inside of the driver's side door.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow lamp on the instrument panel.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle has ABS if there is a yellow ABS warning lamp on the instrument panel.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?

options.text: Press down the brake pedal.
Lift the brake pedal toward you.
Push in the brake knob.
Pull out the brake knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press down the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To stop an air-braked vehicle, press down the brake pedal. Control the pressure so the vehicle stops smoothly and safely.

questions.question: What should you know when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: You should expect to hear any approaching train.
You may not hear a train as it approaches.
You will hear two short blasts of the train's horn.
There will always be flashing warning lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train as it approaches.
questions.explanation: You may not hear an approaching train. Trains may not sound their horn in certain areas, or your vehicle's noise may hide the sound. Do not rely only on warning lights or signals.

questions.question: What is a safety concern right when it starts raining?

options.text: The water will mix with grease and oil on the road, making the roadway slippery.
A driver may forget where the windshield wiper lever is located.
It may stop raining.
People will be using their windshield wipers needlessly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water will mix with grease and oil on the road, making the roadway slippery.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and grease on the road that has not washed away yet.

questions.question: When do spring brakes come on?

options.text: When too much air pressure is lost.
When a control on the dashboard is activated.
When the tires have minimal tread depth.
When the brakes are noisy.

questions.correctAnswerText: When too much air pressure is lost.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure drops too low. Do not wait for this. Exit the road safely and stop your vehicle as soon as you see the low pressure warning.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Stay in the left lane.
Don't drive in the fog.
Use your low beam lights.
Follow the vehicle ahead of you closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't drive in the fog.
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see the road and other hazards. Avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.question: How often should you check secured cargo?

options.text: You may complete an entire trip without checking it.
You can drive at least eight hours without checking it.
You should check it every three hours or 150 miles.
You should not check it.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check it every three hours or 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up
Allow all wheels to lock up
Stop wheels from locking up
Alert other drivers when you are braking

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: After you start your vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Stay on for several minutes.
Turn off within a few seconds.
Stay on until you turn them off.
Remain on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off right away after you start the engine. If a light stays on, your vehicle has a problem.

questions.question: When you exit your vehicle, you must keep ____ parts of your body touching the vehicle at all times.

options.text: One
Four
Three
Two

questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact with it at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: If brake pads create too much heat rubbing against the brake drums:

options.text: The brakes will stick.
The brakes will become extra sensitive.
The brakes may stop working.
The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may stop working.
questions.explanation: Too much heat damages your brakes and makes them less effective. This is called "brake fade." Your brakes may stop working completely.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, which is NOT something you need to do?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Ensure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
Ensure the power steering fluid level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: You must show where the dipstick is and confirm you have enough power steering fluid. The fluid level must be above the refill mark, not above the full mark.

questions.question: One way to handle blind spots is to:

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles so they cannot pass you.
Drive in the left lane so you only worry about vehicles to your right.
Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.
Avoid using your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often and know where other vehicles are.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see where other vehicles are around you. This helps you notice if vehicles are moving into your blind spots.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Respond to the driver's gestures.
Challenge the driver to a race.
Ignore the driver if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore the driver if you can.
questions.explanation: Get away from an aggressive driver if possible. Do not make eye contact, respond to rude gestures, or challenge them.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, you should:

options.text: Assume it is not a problem and keep driving.
Hope the vehicle lasts until someone else drives it.
Stop and check your vehicle to find the problem.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check your vehicle to find the problem.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, stop and inspect your vehicle to find the source.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed by:

options.text: At least one-half.
About one-third.
About one-quarter.
About one-eighth.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least one-half.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by half or more when driving on packed snow. Slippery surfaces make it hard to stop or turn.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will:

options.text: Explain what you know about the inspection process.
Watch someone else inspect your vehicle.
Watch a film about vehicle inspection.
Change all the tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you know about the inspection process.
questions.explanation: You will do a complete inspection of your vehicle and explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: How do you use the controlled braking method?

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels.
Press the brakes with about half force.
Press the brakes until the wheels lock.
Pump the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels. If you need to steer while braking, release the brakes, steer, then press the brakes again.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The tires grip the road better.
The vehicle is easier to control.
The vehicle becomes heavier.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose contact with the road and slide on a layer of water instead.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check how worn the tire is.
Check the windshield wiper fluid level.
Check the tire's air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop soon to make sure the lug nuts are still tight and secure.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) must include all of the following, except:

options.text: The date of the trip.
The route traveled.
The total distance traveled.
The number of stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: The number of stops.
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include: trip dates, starting and ending points, route, odometer readings, total distance, distance in-jurisdiction, and vehicle identification number. The number of stops is not required.

questions.question: Is it legal to send text messages while driving?

options.text: Yes, if the messages are short.
Yes, it is encouraged.
Yes, if asking your employer a question.
No, it is not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is not permitted.
questions.explanation: Sending and reading text messages while driving is prohibited.

questions.question: Most CDL holders have ____ licenses.

options.text: Excepted
Exempted
Non-excepted
Non-exempted

questions.correctAnswerText: Non-excepted
questions.explanation: Most CDL holders who drive commercial vehicles across state lines have non-excepted licenses.

questions.question: When traveling downhill, when should you shift into a lower gear?

options.text: After you start going downhill.
As you go downhill and speed up.
Before you start going downhill.
Near the bottom of the hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going downhill.
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before driving downhill. Shifting at high speed can damage the transmission and prevent engine braking. Choose a safe speed based on the hill's steepness and length, your vehicle's weight, road conditions, and weather.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, first pull straight forward, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
Only if there is empty space in the truck.
Only if hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds.
Only if materials create an inhalation hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show the material class and warn others of potential hazards.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether your vehicle can fit under a bridge, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Swerve as you pass under the bridge.
Slow down.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If unsure about clearance under a bridge, slow down and find an alternate route if possible.

questions.question: When traction is poor, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because it is always best to accelerate slowly.
To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
To avoid driving faster than the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerating too quickly on slippery roads can cause you to lose control. When traction is poor, accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating found?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the dashboard
On the side of each tire
Under the hood

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating shows the maximum safe weight a tire can carry. This information is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, you should:

options.text: Let the engine warm up so fuel reaches it.
Wait for air pressure to build in both brake systems.
Start driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the pedal about 20 times, then start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for air pressure to build in both brake systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, wait for the compressor to build pressure to at least 100 psi in both systems.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rainwater to enter the air tank.
Remove water and oil from the air tank.
Should never be opened.
Must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that can damage the brakes if they build up. Open the air tank drain daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What helps you know when to shift to a higher gear?

options.text: Road speed
Engine speed
Both road speed and engine speed
Neither of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both road speed and engine speed
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift up: engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Check your manual for the correct rpm range, and watch your speedometer to know which speeds work for each gear.

questions.question: When exiting a bus during the vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.
Not touch the handrail.
Hold the handrail firmly.
Rush down the stairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handrail firmly.
questions.explanation: When exiting the bus during the vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. Hold the handrail firmly. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: When driving slower than 40 mph, how many seconds of following distance should you maintain per 10 feet of vehicle length?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: One second
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, maintain one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At higher speeds, add one more second.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:

options.text: Covered with grease.
Covered with coolant.
Covered with oil.
Free of oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil and grease.
questions.explanation: During a brake inspection, check that the shoes and pads have no oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:

options.text: Covered in grease.
Covered in coolant.
Covered in oil.
Free of oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil and grease.
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are broken, missing, or worn too thin.

questions.question: When using mirrors while driving, you should:

options.text: Glance at them briefly.
Look at them for long periods of time.
Use only the rearview mirror.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance at them briefly.
questions.explanation: Looking at mirrors for too long is dangerous. You will travel a long distance without watching the road ahead.
